mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.1% indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad-based consumer demand contraction, reducing corporate revenue expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in HOUST and RSAFS (both below 3-month moving averages) fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%), rising real interest rates compress equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL > 3.0%, SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) above 145,000 thousand persons supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Rank IC for PAYEMS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1500 thousand units signals housing sector contraction, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is below 1500.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal aggressive monetary tightening, raising real interest rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (both above 12-month averages) fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 55% of cases over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During supply shock regimes (INDPRO < 99.0 and CPIAUCSL > 268.0), reduced industrial output and higher input costs erode corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO < 99.0 and CPIAUCSL > 268.0, SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.
